description.value: The study examined brain responses in healthy normal-weight women while viewing photographs of high-calorie foods, low-calorie foods, and nonedible dining-related utensils.

spans.text: Therefore, we applied functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to study the cerebral responses of 13 healthy normal-weight adult women as they viewed color photographs of food.

design.value: Three visual activation tasks were presented over separate scanning runs in a blocked fMRI design: low-calorie foods, high-calorie foods, and nonedible food-related utensils, each contrasted with nonfood control photographs.

spans.text: Three visual activation tasks were presented over separate scanning runs: (1) low-calorie foods, (2) high-calorie foods, and (3) nonedible food-related utensils.
Each of these paradigms lasted for 150 sec, consisting of two 30-sec stimulation periods, which alternated with three control blocks of equal duration.
Following completion of the imaging protocol, subjects exited the scanner room and immediately completed three postscan recognition tests on a personal computer.
